scope: How a team chooses which tests (or test targets) to run for a change so the run stays fast without missing a test the change breaks: the selection methods (build-graph affected-target queries, coverage-based mapping, path filters, predictive selection), how selection fails safe when a change cannot be mapped, which changes select everything (build config, dependencies, shared inputs), the periodic full run, and what evidence a selection decision records so it can be checked. Excluding quarantined tests from the gate belongs to flaky-test-quarantine, suite shape to test-pyramid, and classifying a failed selected test to test-failure-triage; no team-specific layout, tag, selector, path or output contract is researched.
research_type: Technology / software (intent Decide; domain change-based test selection; Technical MEDIUM bar, with every figure on selection recall, missed failures or time saved held to the Statistical MED-HIGH bar: study, sample, measure and result named)

questions.text: Best practices: what is current best practice for this topic?
Known solutions: what solutions, patterns, libraries and tools already exist, and how do they compare?
Platform guidelines: what do the platform owners' own guidelines say, for each platform the topic touches (Apple, Android, Windows, web, the databases and runtimes concerned)?
The expert's view: if we hired an expert consultant in this topic, what would they tell us: what to do, what to avoid, and what people usually get wrong?

methodology.method: guidelines/researching/process/research-methodology-and-sources: orient (domain: change-based regression test selection in CI), go first to the build-system and CI owners' own documentation (Bazel, Nx, Turborepo, Pants, Gradle and Develocity, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure Pipelines, Android TEST_MAPPING, Xcode test plans) and to the published selection studies themselves (Meta, Google TAP, Ekstazi, RTSLinux), then to the selection tools' own READMEs and docs (bazel-diff, target-determinator, Launchable); practitioner sources (Paul Hammant on martinfowler.com, the Mill build blog) only where no primary covers the point; record provenance at generation time.
methodology.search_strategy: WebSearch for each tool's affected / changed / impact-analysis documentation and for the published studies by title; every cited page fetched with WebFetch, PDFs (Memon et al. 2017, Celik et al. 2017, Leong et al. 2019) extracted with pdftotext and quotes checked against the extracted text, with the PDF ligatures (fi, ff) restored to the printed words.
methodology.inclusion: Official documentation of the build systems, CI services and selection tools; peer-reviewed or archived papers reporting industrial or open-source selection results with sample and measure disclosed; vendor documentation for the vendor's own product behaviour; practitioner articles only for experience no primary source covers, flagged in trust basis.
methodology.exclusion: Search-result snippets; tutorial and content-farm posts surfaced by search (qaskills.sh, oneuptime.com, graphite guides) whose claims were not traceable to a primary; pages that could not be read (the Google Testing Blog 'Efficacy Presubmit' body, the CloudBees Smart Tests observation page, which returned 404); any claim not backed by a fetched quote.
methodology.scoring: guidelines/researching/evidence/verification-and-trust-scoring: Authority 30 + Independent corroboration 25 + Accuracy/verifiability 20 + Currency 10 + Transparency 15, capped by the Technical MEDIUM ceiling for tool behaviour and by the Statistical MED-HIGH bar for figures; vendor claims about their own commercial products are discounted for conflict of interest; independence counted multi-independent only when two independent publishers hold the quoted words, so claims corroborated in substance but not in wording are marked single with the corroboration named in basis.

summary: Only one of the five listed rules holds at its stated strength: fail-closed-when-unsure is supported at SHOULD. Every safe-selection tool read here falls back to selecting everything when it cannot map a change: Azure TIA, bazel-diff, Turborepo on a shallow checkout, GitHub Actions when the diff times out, GitLab when there is no push event. The research literature defines a safe technique as one that selects all affected tests. The other four rules state their checks as fails, i.e. MUST. The sources support them only at SHOULD. Tools record why each test was selected (Develocity, Nx --explain, target-determinator -verbose) and treat every changed file as a correctness input (bazel-diff), but none requires a written justification per selection, a written account of every changed path, or a statement of each fallback. Tools also legitimately select tests for reasons outside the diff: previously failing, new, changed or flaky tests. No source speaks to reasoning from commit messages; tools select from the changed files and, at best, their content hashes. The research finds ten practices no listed rule covers: a change of unknown reach selects everything; shared inputs such as lockfiles and build config select everything; selection follows the dependency graph, not paths alone; diff against a known-good base; run the full suite periodically or after merge; always select new, changed and recently failing tests; validate selection against full runs; record why each test was selected; measure selection recall and savings with a named study; and path-skipped required checks must be handled. Published figures: Meta reports at least 95% of individual test failures and 99.9% of faulty changes still caught at half the testing cost; Google TAP saw 63K of 5.5 million affected test targets ever fail in a month; Ekstazi cut end-to-end test time by 32% on average across 615 revisions of 32 projects.
open_questions: How often the periodic full run happens and where: Azure TIA leaves the periodicity configurable, Launchable names post-merge and nightly, Develocity names nightly and pre-release, and Google TAP runs all affected targets per milestone (about every 45 minutes); the owner decides whether the rule names one cadence or requires the team to set and record one.

Whether predictive (machine-learned) selection may gate a merge on its own, or only run pre-merge with a deterministic or full run behind it: Meta and Develocity accept a bounded miss rate, while the safe-selection literature does not.

Whether each-selection-justified-by-diff, every-changed-path-accounted-for, fail-closed-is-stated and reasoning-cites-diff-contents keep their fail (MUST) strength as team checks or are restated at the SHOULD strength the sources support.
Whether a test selected for a reason outside the diff (previously failing, newly added, recently flaky, as Azure TIA and Develocity do) counts as justified under each-selection-justified-by-diff.

Which file classes a team may declare as unable to affect tests (Azure TIA's TIA_IncludePathFilters exclusions, GitHub paths-ignore), and who approves that list, since every exclusion narrows a fail-safe fallback.

Which shared inputs select everything in the cookbook's general rule (lockfiles, build and CI configuration, toolchains, shared test fixtures): the tools differ, with Nx defaulting a lockfile change to every task and Pants treating a lockfile change as changing all users of any dependency.
limitations: Google TAP has no public product documentation; its selection behaviour is taken from Memon et al. (ICSE-SEIP 2017) and Leong et al. (ICSE-SEIP 2019), read from copies hosted by a university course page and an author's site. The Google Testing Blog post 'Efficacy Presubmit' (2018-09-17) returned its title but not its body, so it is not cited.
Buck2's own documentation on changed-target selection was not fetched; Buck2 is not covered beyond what the Bazel-family tools show.

Azure DevOps Test Impact Analysis covers only managed .NET Framework code on a single machine (.NET Core and multi-machine topologies are unsupported) and its body dates from 2018 though the page was updated 2026-05-07; its behaviour is current for the product but narrow.

Launchable is now published as CloudBees Smart Tests; the CloudBees observation-mode page returned 404, so Launchable's own help site was used. Launchable, Develocity and Meta's figures are vendor- or owner-reported and not independently replicated.

The GitHub Actions page's exact wording of its changed-file limit for path filters was not captured verbatim, so no claim rests on it; the GitLab CI YAML reference was read from character 170000 on for rules:changes only.
PDF text was extracted with pdftotext, which drops fi and ff ligatures; quotes restore the printed words (e.g. 'affected', 'find').

Apple's Xcode documentation says nothing about change-based selection; Android's guidance is limited to TEST_MAPPING directory and file-pattern rules for presubmit; no Windows guidance applies beyond Azure DevOps.
No source was found that addresses selection judgments resting on commit messages or branch names, so reasoning-cites-diff-contents could be neither supported nor contradicted on that point.
license: MIT (this research record); quoted material remains under its sources' terms and is quoted for verification.
